active_paradigms.idea: Replace score-only random beam search with exact target-layout reconstruction using CP-SAT, then use a deterministic sliding-puzzle realization
active_paradigms.description: The current program first moves the blank to the lower-right corner and then performs a broad stochastic beam search over moves. Its state evaluation correctly computes the largest acyclic connected component, but it ranks states mostly by largest-tree size minus a very large total-component penalty, rather than by the official score. This is effective at finding large partial trees, explaining the approximately 435k result, but it has no explicit representation of a complete target arrangement and is unlikely to cross the discontinuity from S=N^2-2 to S=N^2-1. Model every board cell as a variable selecting one input tile occurrence, with all-different constraints and exact horizontal/vertical port-consistency constraints. Require no ports to leave the board or point into the blank, require exactly N^2-2 matched edges, and enforce connectivity through a rooted flow/arborescence constraint; these conditions make the painted graph a spanning tree. Add the blank at a chosen corner and solve several layouts, preferring layouts whose tile permutation has compatible sliding-puzzle parity. Once a complete layout is obtained, use a standard layer-by-layer tile-routing procedure that locks completed rows and columns and handles the final two rows/columns jointly; this has O(N^3) moves and is designed to fit the given 2N^3 budget. This directly attacks the enormous full-tree score bonus, where any valid full tree scores at least 500000 and shorter realizations score substantially more.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary goal is obtaining S=N^2-1 reliably; after that, minimize K because full-tree score is 500000*(2-K/T), whereas all incomplete states are capped below 500000.
active_paradigms.cautions: The tiles are occurrences, not merely 16 mask types, so duplicate masks need distinct assignment variables until a final reachable permutation is selected. A connected graph with N^2-1 vertices and N^2-2 edges is automatically a tree, but port matching must also forbid unmatched internal and boundary stubs. Sliding-puzzle reachability has a parity invariant; exploit swaps of equal-mask occurrences or enumerate blank corners/layout alternatives to repair parity without changing the picture. Do not assume the arbitrary CP-SAT layout can always be routed within T unless the routing move count is explicitly measured.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a target-aware shortest-path search in permutation space after generating candidate tree layouts, rather than a history-deduplicated score beam
active_paradigms.description: The present beam maintains only 250 states for N=10, forbids immediate reversals, globally discards a board whenever it was reached earlier, and samples much of the next beam randomly. Those choices save time, but they eliminate routes that temporarily lower tree quality and are often necessary to position the blank for a final tile-placement maneuver. In particular, its global transposition table is unsafe as a diversity mechanism: the same board reached at a slightly greater depth can have a different useful history context, and retaining only one path strongly collapses the beam around similar local optima. Given one or several valid target layouts from a tree-layout generator, run weighted A* or best-first search whose state cost is actual move count and whose heuristic is a tile-to-target lower bound. Use Manhattan distance summed over tiles, divided by two, augmented by blank-to-next-required-tile distance; for duplicate tile masks use the minimum bipartite matching distance between current and target occurrences. Search toward a target layout, not toward the intermediate graph score, and retain incumbent complete solutions so the search can stop safely before the time limit. If exact A* is too wide, use a bounded transposition table keyed by board plus last move and apply beam pruning only by f=g+w*h, with occasional diversity buckets based on blank position and number of correctly placed tiles. This method converts the problem from unguided hill climbing on S into a directed attempt to reverse the generator's scramble or reach an equivalent full-tree arrangement.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Minimize K conditional on a known full-tree target, while preserving enough state diversity to reach S=N^2-1 instead of maximizing only partial-tree S.
active_paradigms.cautions: A raw Manhattan heuristic is not admissible when several tiles share a mask; compute an assignment lower bound for duplicates or use labeled occurrences consistently. Do not use the current artificial lower-right blank relocation as a mandatory prefix, because it may spend moves and destroy useful near-target structure. Include the last move in duplicate detection if reverse-move pruning is retained, and cap memory tightly because the board state space is huge. A search that fails to reach a target must still output the best verified partial-tree path, evaluated with the official largest-tree calculation.

active_paradigms.idea: Exploit the known generator distribution with reverse-scramble likelihood and particle filtering over candidate original trees
active_paradigms.description: Every input is not an arbitrary tile multiset: it was made by first generating a random spanning tree with the blank at the lower-right corner, then applying exactly T non-immediately-reversing random blank moves. The current program ignores this very strong prior and treats all graph-improving arrangements as equally plausible. Maintain a population of complete tree-layout hypotheses that satisfy tile-port constraints, and score each hypothesis by how plausibly the observed board could be obtained from it under T random sliding moves. The likelihood proxy should emphasize tile displacement, blank displacement, and preservation of local tile adjacencies that a length-T random walk is unlikely to accidentally reconstruct; select hypotheses with low estimated routing cost from the observed state. For each selected hypothesis, perform a short reverse-directed particle rollout: moves are sampled toward correcting mismatched tile positions, but particles are resampled by a combined target-distance and official-tree score. Unlike the existing one-path-per-hash beam, this keeps multiple incompatible explanations of the hidden original picture and can discover the actual generator layout, whose reverse scramble is guaranteed to be within T moves. Once a particle reaches a full tree, immediately retain it and spend remaining time reducing K with local path shortening, such as removing loops between repeated board hashes. This is fundamentally distribution-aware: it seeks the original hidden solution rather than merely any local increase in matched ports.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Increase the probability of finding a guaranteed-within-budget full tree by recovering an original-like layout; among recovered layouts, reduce K by selecting the lowest estimated reverse-scramble distance.
active_paradigms.cautions: The generator random walk is long enough that exact probability computation is impractical, so use the likelihood only as a ranking signal, never as a correctness test. Candidate layouts must still be checked with the exact tree evaluator and every emitted move must be simulated. Preserve a deterministic fallback because stochastic particle methods have variance across the 50 public cases. Path-loop removal is valid only when the board configuration, including blank location, repeats exactly; do not remove a segment based solely on equal picture score or equal blank position.
